title: Practical Performance
welcome_lead: Today's adventure: Practical Performance in GCSE PE.
meta_desc: GCSE PE adventure on Practical Performance.
final_note: You worked through the key terms in Practical Performance.

concepts.def: A learned action aimed at achieving a result with maximum certainty and efficiency, usually with minimum effort, developed through practice.
A skill affected by an unpredictable environment, such as a tackle in rugby, where the performer must constantly adapt to opponents and conditions.
A self-paced skill performed in a stable, predictable environment, such as a golf putt, where the technique stays largely the same each time.
Practising a skill in its complete form without breaking it down, suitable for simple skills that cannot easily be split into parts.
Breaking a complex skill into sections and practising each separately before linking them, useful for difficult or dangerous skills.
Information about performance from an outside source such as a coach, teammate or video, important for beginners who cannot yet judge their own technique.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Practical Performance — a core area of GCSE PE.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Practical Performance brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Practical Performance.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: A golf putt is best classified as a:
options: Open skill
Closed skill
Externally paced skill
Reaction skill

mcqs.q: Part practice is most useful for:
options: Very simple skills
Complex or dangerous skills
Skills that cannot be divided
Expert performers only

mcqs.q: Feedback from a coach is an example of:
options: Intrinsic feedback
Extrinsic feedback
Negative feedback only
Kinaesthetic feedback

mcqs.q: An open skill requires the performer to:
options: Repeat the same fixed movement
Adapt to a changing environment
Ignore opponents
Stay completely self-paced

mcqs.q: Is a golf putt an open or closed skill?
options: Only for skills that cannot be divided.
Open, because golf is played outdoors.
It is a gross skill, so it must be open.
Closed - it is self-paced in a stable environment.

mcqs.q: When is part practice better than whole practice?
options: For complex or dangerous skills that can be broken into sections.
For every skill, because more breaks are always better.
Only for skills that cannot be divided.
It is a gross skill, so it must be open.

mcqs.q: Why do beginners rely on extrinsic feedback?
options: Beginners should only use intrinsic feedback.
Feedback slows beginners down.
It is a gross skill, so it must be open.
They cannot yet judge their own performance using internal cues.
